findings.title: getSubGroupsCount returns null when group is concurrently deleted
findings.body: When the group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and the method now returns null instead of throwing an NPE. The `Long` return type is documented and used as a count. Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` pass the result to `representation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, and other callers may unbox it, so an NPE can resurface further up the stack. Returning 0, or treating the group as gone, would be safer. The other delegating methods (`getSubGroupsStream(...)`) still call `modelSupplier.get()` without a null check, so the same race remains there.

findings.title: Concurrency test thread is not joined and is racy
findings.body: The reader thread is started but never joined, so `caughtExceptions` can be asserted while the thread is still running, or before it has done any reads. The thread is not a daemon and can outlive the test. If the loop is slow, no read may overlap the deletes at all, so the test can pass without exercising the race. It should join the thread before the assertion and ensure that reads happen during the deletes.

findings.title: Test does not exercise the subGroupsCount path that was fixed
findings.body: The test calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. That is the brief representation and the fifth argument may not request `subGroupsCount`. The fix is in `getSubGroupsCount`, so the test may not cover the changed code path.
